answers.q1: Mars, the fourth planet from the Sun, is known for its reddish color caused by iron oxide on its surface. It has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, and features the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons. Scientists study Mars closely because its ancient rivers and lakebeds suggest it may once have supported liquid water.
Uranus rotates on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees, so its poles take turns pointing almost directly at the Sun during its very long orbit.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, a gas giant so massive that its Great Red Spot, a storm larger than Earth, has been raging for at least 350 years.
Venus has a thick, toxic atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide, which traps heat so effectively that its surface is hotter than Mercury's despite being farther from the Sun.
Saturn is best known for its spectacular ring system, made up of countless particles of ice and rock ranging in size from tiny grains to chunks as large as a house.
Earth is the only known planet to host life, thanks in part to liquid oceans, a protective magnetic field, and an atmosphere rich in nitrogen and oxygen.

Because its ancient rivers and lakebeds suggest liquid water may once have existed, scientists closely study Mars. Known for a reddish color caused by iron oxide on its surface, Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. The largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, is a feature of Mars, which also has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
Mercury is the smallest and innermost planet, with almost no atmosphere to retain heat, so its surface swings between extreme daytime highs and freezing nighttime lows.
Neptune is the most distant major planet, a cold blue world whose supersonic winds are among the fastest ever recorded anywhere in our corner of space.
